samples.rationale: The fix clamps at the HTTP boundary (`int effectivePage = Math.max(page, 1);`) and threads one value into both `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName(effectivePage, lastName)` and `addPaginationModel(effectivePage, ...)`, so query and view agree — minimal, in-place, no new type. Clamping inside `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName` would have been a single seam instead of two call sites a future caller can miss; the two-line comment mostly restates the code. The test is behavior-named (`theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsBelowOne`), CSV-parameterized over 0 and -5, phase-separated, and asserts the observable outcome (`status().isOk()`, `currentPage` 1). It violates the factory rule with a bare `new Owner()` and leaves mystery literals in `PageRequest.of(0, 5)`. No documentation visible in the patch is made stale.

The fix clamps once into `effectivePage` and threads it to both `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName(effectivePage, lastName)` and `addPaginationModel(effectivePage, ...)`, so query and view cannot diverge; it sits in the controller alongside existing pagination handling, which reads as request normalization rather than a new domain rule, though pushing the clamp into the private paging helper would have been tighter. `effectivePage` is well named and the explanatory comment matches surrounding style. The test name `theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsBelowOne` follows the BDD school and the CsvSource covers 0 and -5, but it constructs `new Owner()` directly instead of a factory, leaves `PageRequest.of(0, 5)`'s page size as a mystery literal, and pins behavior partly through a Mockito `verify`. No documentation visible in the patch is made stale.

The clamp is minimal and correct — `int effectivePage = Math.max(page, 1)` feeds both `findPaginatedForOwnersLastName(effectivePage, ...)` and `addPaginationModel(effectivePage, ...)`, so query and view agree — but it adds another normalization rule to a controller the architecture brief says holds none, and the recorded deviation list does not cover it; a page-clamping seam below the web layer would have been unit-testable. The test name `theOwnerListShouldShowFirstPageWhenPageIsBelowOne` follows the BDD school and phases are blank-line separated, yet `new Owner()` bypasses the required factory method, `PageRequest.of(0, 5)` embeds an unnamed page-size literal, and `verify(this.owners)` asserts a collaborator interaction rather than owned behavior. The redundant comment restates `Math.max`.
